builds.howItPlays: You spend the early turns clearing your opponent's units with cheap removal like Flurry of Blades, which deals 1 to every unit at the battlefields, and Blood Money, while spells like Catalyst of Aeons give you extra runes. Once you can afford Dazzling Aurora, a 9-cost gear that plays the next unit from the top of your deck for free at the end of each of your turns, you put Harnessed Dragon (kills an enemy unit when it arrives) and Elder Dragon (10 Might) on the battlefields and hold them for your points.
builds.whyYou: You like a long game where you spend the first half answering whatever your opponent plays and hardly attack at all. You're happy to play spells that give you extra runes instead of units, because you know that once your huge units arrive your opponent can't keep up. You don't mind that the free unit from Dazzling Aurora is whatever sits on top of your deck, since every unit in the deck is big. If surviving the early turns and then taking over the board sounds better to you than racing, this Poppy suits you.

Cards that decided each Axis. Pace: no units costing 2 or less, and 13 to 15 cards costing 5+ (Dazzling Aurora, Elder Dragon, Harnessed Dragon, Rift Herald). Stance: 12 to 13 answers (Flurry of Blades, Blood Money, Cull the Weak, Divine Judgment or The Ruination, Sabotage, Salvage) against 1 to 3 pressure cards, with 24 to 26 own-plan cards. Formula and judgment were within 1.5 on every Axis (scorer pace 0.5 to 1 against judged 2). Legend ability: when you hold, gain 1 XP; spend 3 XP and exhaust to draw 1. Also played: none. Hartford and Utrecht RQ Best-of lists vouch for the style but are illegal (Aspirant's Climb) and were not scored. Confidence: low. Reviewer: the Barcelona claim is a repost with no system-account deck; the Aurora engine is a single 3-of, so check that no ban has touched Dazzling Aurora or Catalyst of Aeons.

builds.howItPlays: You put cheap units on the battlefields early and win their fights with Punch First, which gives a unit +5 Might for the turn, and Grim Resolve, and every battlefield you hold gives Poppy XP that she spends to draw you cards. Shepherd's Heirloom, a 2-cost gear that gives a unit +2 Might, and Master Yi, Tempered, a 4-cost unit that earns 2 XP each time it takes or holds a battlefield, keep the XP coming until your units can hold for the last points.
builds.whyYou: You like having units on the board from the first turns and winning the fights over each battlefield instead of waiting for a big late play. You enjoy the small edges that build up: a combat trick at the right moment, a bit of XP here and there, an extra card from Poppy most turns. You'd rather keep up steady pressure than bet the game on one swing, and you don't mind a game that runs into the middle turns as long as you're ahead on the board. If pushing hard with sturdy units and a trick in hand sounds fun, this Poppy suits you.
